A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hard View Selection work. The complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison despite the revised title and added appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original ImageNet and transfer-task experiments, augmentation analyses, adversarial-learning experiments, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds iBOT results, runtime measurements, and qualitative attention-map comparisons.

M1.justification: The sampled-view, sample-wise maximum-loss selection and subsequent training procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 now explicitly forwards views before forming pairs, consistent with the N view embeddings already described in v1 Section 3.2. No new HVS component is established.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet, CIFAR10/100, Flowers102, Food101, iNaturalist 2021, VOC07+12, and COCO for the same tasks. The added iBOT evaluation and attention examples reuse ImageNet coverage; the resolution tests concern experimental settings.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds iBOT ViT-S/16, evaluated with and without HVS at 100 and 300 epochs. The existing DINO, SimSiam, SimCLR, manual-policy, and STN comparison sets are retained, making this a limited comparator expansion.

E3.justification: New Appendix H adds timing tests halving DINO global/local resolutions from 224/96 to 112/48 and SimSiam resolution from 224 to 112. Appendix J compares attention from 100-epoch DINO ViT-S/16 models on ImageNet validation images. Existing accuracy-evaluation protocols and Appendix G settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix H adds a brief reduced-resolution runtime investigation, and Appendix J adds a qualitative comparison of HVS and baseline attention maps. These supplement the retained IoU, color, view-count, manual-policy, STN, longer-training, and easy-selection analyses.

E5.justification: Section 4 replaces 'multiple seeds' with three seeds, except two for iBOT. This specifies run counts without establishing that existing experiments received additional runs. Previously stated counts for other analyses remain, and no new confidence intervals or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises 300-epoch DINO RN50+HVS linear/k-NN scores from 75.80/70.11 to 75.65/70.05. New iBOT linear results are 69.50 versus 70.41 at 100 epochs and 72.48 versus 73.99 at 300 epochs. Appendix H adds reduced-resolution timings of 0.52 to 0.38 seconds per batch for DINO and 0.20 to 0.16 for SimSiam. Existing transfer and ablation results are retained.

T1.justification: The main mathematical objectives and the SimCLR formulation are retained, with the latter moved from Appendix H to Appendix I. Its rewritten explanation supplies intuition rather than a new definition, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract revises its quoted ImageNet improvement figures from 0.55% and 1.9% to 0.40% and 1.9%. Applicability is explicitly framed as SSL and includes iBOT, while the central contribution remains unchanged; v1 already evaluated non-contrastive DINO and SimSiam.

C2.justification: V3 links zooming patterns to local-to-global correspondence and suggests multi-crop differences explain poor transfer of manual IoU policies between methods. Appendix H adds memory and efficiency qualifications. Appendix J acknowledges mostly similar attention maps while suggesting occasional differences in object shape and contextual attention.

D1.justification: Appendix H newly details DINO's four global and sixteen local candidate views, the retained 128-comparison cap, and sequential selection/backpropagation memory use. Table 13 supplies timing hardware and software, including RTX 3080, PyTorch 2.0.1, and CUDA 11.8. Existing hyperparameter tables and the code-access statement are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds the iBOT citation and sharpens its comparison with Tian et al. (2020b), emphasizing current-model-state selection and IoU analysis. It also removes the validation-loss characterization of MADAug. These refine positioning within the existing related-work coverage.

P1.justification: The title changes from contrastive to self-supervised learning, the review header disappears, and selected introduction, related-work, and explanatory passages are rewritten. New overhead and attention appendices are inserted, with the objectives appendix renumbered. The main narrative and section order remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V3 substantially expands the visual presentation with paired, per-head attention comparisons in Figures 12–20, a new overhead table, and iBOT rows in Table 1. It also relocates Figure 3 and Table 4 and regroups appendix hyperparameter tables. Existing plots are reused rather than redrawn.

improvement.justification: The iBOT comparison strengthens support for applicability, while explicit seed counts and hardware-specific timing measurements improve transparency. The attention study appropriately acknowledges limited qualitative differences. These are useful but bounded gains: reduced-resolution speed tests lack corresponding accuracy measurements, and the new iBOT results lack dedicated hyperparameter documentation.
